item.title: Florida Freeze Triggers Widespread Snook Kill, Raising Concerns for Inshore Fisheries
item.description: A recent Florida freeze has triggered widespread snook mortality, with anglers reporting dead and cold-stunned fish across inshore waters. Biologists are still assessing the full impact on snook populations. The post Florida Freeze Triggers Widespread Snook Kill, Raising Concerns for Inshore Fisheries first appeared on Coastal Angler & The Angler Magazine.

item.title: Fishing for Monster Winter Bass on Lake Guntersville
item.description: Lake Guntersville, Alabama, is legendary among bass anglers nationwide—and for good reason. Consistently ranked as one of the top bass fisheries in the U.S. and host of the 2014 Bassmaster Classic, Guntersville is famous for producing giant largemouth bass, especially from late winter through early spring. The post Fishing for Monster Winter Bass on Lake Guntersville first appeared on Coastal Angler & The Angler Magazine.

item.title: Endless Wishes: Why the Ultimate Bucket-List Fishing Trip Is Right Outside My Door
item.description: What if the ultimate bucket-list fishing trip didn’t require a passport? From offshore pelagics to back-bay favorites, Southwest Florida offers endless opportunities—every day of the year. Capt. Kevin Deiter reflects on why the best fishing adventures might be closer to home than you think. The post Endless Wishes: Why the Ultimate Bucket-List Fishing Trip Is Right Outside My Door first appeared on Coastal Angler & The Angler Magazine.

item.title: Unknown Giants of the Mediterranean
item.description: Mallorca, a small island in the Mediterranean Sea next to the Strait of Gibraltar. It´s a place where nobody expects much. item.title: Hook, Line & Dine in New Orleans: Venice Yellowfin to a Commander’s Palace Feast
item.description: We ran offshore from Venice at dawn, boxed up Gulf yellowfin by midday, and ended the day at Commander’s Palace—where our fresh catch became a true New Orleans feast. The post Hook, Line & Dine in New Orleans: Venice Yellowfin to a Commander’s Palace Feast first appeared on Coastal Angler & The Angler Magazine.

item.title: Florida Anglers Cheer Potential 39-Day Atlantic Red Snapper Season After Years of Short Closures
item.description: Anglers and fishing charter operators along Florida’s Atlantic coast are celebrating a major step toward a longer recreational Atlantic red snapper season in 2026, potentially ending years of very short seasons under federal limits. The post Florida Anglers Cheer Potential 39-Day Atlantic Red Snapper Season After Years of Short Closures first appeared on Coastal Angler & The Angler Magazine.
